msg: assignment discards 'const' qualifier from pointer target type (CType(CPointer(CUnsigned(CLong())),true,false,false) = CType(CPointer(CUnsigned(CLong())),false,false,true))
reasoning: FALSE POSITIVE: 76baeebf7df.c (Linux NUMA). 'Assignment discards const qualifier' at lines 133-137, when def(NUMA) AND def(PCI) AND !def(const). The condition '!def(const)' means the alarm fires when the 'const' keyword is not defined as a macro. In standard C, 'const' is a language keyword, not a macro — it is always 'defined' in the sense that it is always available. This is a tool artifact: when the family analysis treats 'const' as an undeclared identifier (i.e., !def(const)), it removes the const qualifier from types, causing spurious const-discarding warnings. Under normal compilation, no const is discarded in this code.
